subject: Warning message in Lavaan (not standard errors)

messages.author: d2bffd1a5d780ca8
messages.subject: Warning message in Lavaan (not standard errors)
parts:
Hello guys,

I've experienced some troubles when fitting uncorrelated and bifactor models using Lavaan. My database consists of a three-point Likert scale with 830 subjects, so, I wouldn't believe the sample size is causing the problem. There are no missing values, but the data is non-normal. Therefore, I chose to declare it as ordered in order to use WLSMV (default option in Lavaan). Also, there are no identification problems (i.e. number of pieces of information > parameters to be estimated). I already checked the dataset for unusual values, uninstall R/RStudio and reinstalling again including all the packages, but nothing works.

I would really appreciate your help. Perhaps it's some minor mistake I can't find.

Thanks in advance. Best regards,

Here is my code:

uncorrel <- ' 
F1 =~ b5+b10+b13
F2 =~ b2+b7+b8+b11
F3 =~ b3+b6+b12
F4 =~ b4+b9
F1 ~~ 0*F2
F1 ~~ 0*F3
F1 ~~ 0*F4
F2 ~~ 0*F3
F2 ~~ 0*F4
F3 ~~ 0*F4'

bifactor <- '
GF =~ b2+b3+b4+b5+b6+b7+b8+b9+b10+b11+b12+b13
F1 =~ b5+b10+b13
F2 =~ b2+b7+b8+b11
F3 =~ b3+b6+b12
F4 =~ b4+b9
F1 ~~ 0*F2
F1 ~~ 0*F3
F1 ~~ 0*F4
F2 ~~ 0*F3
F2 ~~ 0*F4
F3 ~~ 0*F4
GF ~~ 0*F1
GF ~~ 0*F2
GF ~~ 0*F3
GF ~~ 0*F4'

bifactor.fit <- cfa(bifactor, data = mydata, ordered = paste0("b", 2:13))
uncorrel.fit <- cfa(uncorrel, data = mydata, ordered = paste0("b", 2:13))

The warning messages are:

1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats, : lavaan WARNING: Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not identified.
2: In lav_test_satorra_bentler(lavobject = NULL, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats, : lavaan WARNING: could not invert information matrix needed for robust test statistic

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Warning message in Lavaan (not standard errors)
parts:
Both models are not statistically identified because (a) factor F4 has only two indicators and (b) factor F4 is uncorrelated with everything else in the model. A common factor must have at least 3 indicators unless the factor is correlated with something else in the model. The warning message is correct.
     See, e.g., Bollen's (1989) classic text, or Rigdon (1995)
Bollen, K. A. (1989). Structural equations with latent variables Wiley. New York.  
Rigdon, E. E. (1995). A necessary and sufficient identification rule for structural models estimated in practice. Multivariate behavioral research, 30(3), 359-383.  

--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Warning message in Lavaan (not standard errors)
parts: The surprising problem with an uncorrelated factor occurs because covariances between observed variables loading on different common factors are equal to the product of the two loadings times the correlation between the common factors. If the factor correlation is 0, then the correlation between the observed variables is also 0, and you can't use that correlation to solve for the loadings. If a factor has p = 3 indicators, there are p * (p+1) / 2 = 6 variance and covariances among the 3 observed variables, and that lets you solve for the 3 loadings + 3 residual variances "internally," without needing any other information. (Here, to keep this simple, I assume that the factor's variance is constrained.) But with only 2 indicators, there are only 3 variances and covariances among them, which is not enough to solve for the 2 loadings + 2 residual variances, so you either need more information (from covariances with other variables) or constraints to reduce the number of free parameters.

messages.subject: Re: Warning message in Lavaan (not standard errors)
parts:
I see. Thanks again Dr. for your kind and clarifying response.

Have a nice day.
El mar, 29 dic 2020 a las 9:31, Edward Rigdon (<edward...@gmail.com>) escribió:

The surprising problem with an uncorrelated factor occurs because covariances between observed variables loading on different common factors are equal to the product of the two loadings times the correlation between the common factors. If the factor correlation is 0, then the correlation between the observed variables is also 0, and you can't use that correlation to solve for the loadings. If a factor has p = 3 indicators, there are p * (p+1) / 2 = 6 variance and covariances among the 3 observed variables, and that lets you solve for the 3 loadings + 3 residual variances "internally," without needing any other information. (Here, to keep this simple, I assume that the factor's variance is constrained.) But with only 2 indicators, there are only 3 variances and covariances among them, which is not enough to solve for the 2 loadings + 2 residual variances, so you either need more information (from covariances with other variables) or constraints to reduce the number of free parameters.

On Tue, Dec 29, 2020 at 9:01 AM Juan Diego Hernández Lalinde <hernandez...@gmail.com> wrote:
I was aware of that option of constraining some parameters, but I was unaware of that identification problem when fitting models in which are uncorrelated factors with only two indicators.

Thanks again, Dr. Rigdon. 

Best regards.

El mar., 29 de diciembre de 2020 08:24, Edward Rigdon <edward...@gmail.com> escribió:
You can make such a model, with only two indicators and an uncorrelated factor, identified by imposing an equality constraint--either constraining the loadings to equality or constraining the residual variances to equality. You might also achieve identification by fixing one residual variance to a specific value. At the limit of identifiability, it will be hard to tell whether such a constraint is really consistent with the data, or not. The default constraint of fixing a loading to 1 does not help here--it (or an equivalent) is already necessary to address a more fundamental identification problem in common factor models, regardless of the number of indicators.

On Tue, Dec 29, 2020 at 8:16 AM Juan Diego Hernández Lalinde <hernandez...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello Dr. Ridgon,

Thank you very much for your quick response.

I introduced some changes in the models by adding a third indicator to factor F4 and, voilá, it worked perfectly. I appreciate so much your help, but, what can I do if the theory stablish the model this way, with only two items in this particulary factor?

Thanks again.

El lun., 28 de diciembre de 2020 21:17, Edward Rigdon <edward...@gmail.com> escribió:
     Both models are not statistically identified because (a) factor F4 has only two indicators and (b) factor F4 is uncorrelated with everything else in the model. A common factor must have at least 3 indicators unless the factor is correlated with something else in the model. The warning message is correct.
     See, e.g., Bollen's (1989) classic text, or Rigdon (1995)
Bollen, K. A. (1989). Structural equations with latent variables Wiley. New York.  
Rigdon, E. E. (1995). A necessary and sufficient identification rule for structural models estimated in practice. Multivariate behavioral research, 30(3), 359-383.  

--Ed Rigdon



On Mon, Dec 28, 2020 at 8:54 PM Juan Diego Hernández Lalinde <hernandez...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello guys,

I've experienced some troubles when fitting uncorrelated and bifactor models using Lavaan. My database consists of a three-point Likert scale with 830 subjects, so, I wouldn't believe the sample size is causing the problem. There are no missing values, but the data is non-normal. Therefore, I chose to declare it as ordered in order to use WLSMV (default option in Lavaan). Also, there are no identification problems (i.e. number of pieces of information > parameters to be estimated). I already checked the dataset for unusual values, uninstall R/RStudio and reinstalling again including all the packages, but nothing works.

I would really appreciate your help. Perhaps it's some minor mistake I can't find.

Thanks in advance. Best regards,

Here is my code:

uncorrel <- ' 
F1 =~ b5+b10+b13
F2 =~ b2+b7+b8+b11
F3 =~ b3+b6+b12
F4 =~ b4+b9
F1 ~~ 0*F2
F1 ~~ 0*F3
F1 ~~ 0*F4
F2 ~~ 0*F3
F2 ~~ 0*F4
F3 ~~ 0*F4'

bifactor <- '
GF =~ b2+b3+b4+b5+b6+b7+b8+b9+b10+b11+b12+b13
F1 =~ b5+b10+b13
F2 =~ b2+b7+b8+b11
F3 =~ b3+b6+b12
F4 =~ b4+b9
F1 ~~ 0*F2
F1 ~~ 0*F3
F1 ~~ 0*F4
F2 ~~ 0*F3
F2 ~~ 0*F4
F3 ~~ 0*F4
GF ~~ 0*F1
GF ~~ 0*F2
GF ~~ 0*F3
GF ~~ 0*F4'

bifactor.fit <- cfa(bifactor, data = mydata, ordered = paste0("b", 2:13))
uncorrel.fit <- cfa(uncorrel, data = mydata, ordered = paste0("b", 2:13))

The warning messages are:

1: In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats, : lavaan WARNING: Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not identified.
2: In lav_test_satorra_bentler(lavobject = NULL, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats, : lavaan WARNING: could not invert information matrix needed for robust test statistic
